reviews.decision_reason: select_demand_records is the only assigned unit whose declared role can account for dropping input record n06-r07 while retaining lower-demand n06-r08. The assigned input contains n06-r07 with demand_score 4 and n06-r08 with demand_score 3, but the assigned output needs/evidence_sources include n06-r08 and omit n06-r07. The package does not provide market-demand evidence that would justify preferring the lower-scored record, so the selection is behaviorally significant and propagates to the downstream final_output priorities.

No evidence in the supplied semantic package shows a normalization defect. The records that appear in assigned_job_output preserve record_id, source_id, source_weight, need, and demand_score consistently with assigned_job_input; the observed behavioral fault is the missing/extra record selection, not value normalization.

assemble_provenance appears to assemble the selected records consistently: metadata counts match the seven emitted needs and evidence_sources, ranks are deterministic, and stdout matches assigned_job_output. The package does not show this unit independently causing the unsupported lower-demand substitution.
